title: The Most Chaotic Olympic Marathon Ever

scenes.narration: The 1904 Olympic marathon may have been the most ridiculous race in Olympic history.
It was held in St. Louis on a brutally hot, dusty afternoon, over roads filled with hills, traffic, and choking clouds of dirt.
And almost immediately, things went wrong.
One runner was chased off course by wild dogs.
Another stopped at an orchard and ate some peaches.
A Cuban competitor showed up in street clothes, cut his trousers into shorts, and reportedly stopped along the route for food.
After becoming exhausted, Lorz got into a car and rode for roughly eleven miles.
When the car broke down, he started running again, entered the stadium first, and was briefly treated as the winner before officials discovered what happened.
But the actual winner, Thomas Hicks, had an even stranger race.
His trainers gave him egg whites, brandy—and small doses of strychnine, a substance now known as a deadly poison but then sometimes used as a stimulant.
By the final miles, Hicks could barely move.
His trainers helped keep him going until he crossed the finish line in 3 hours and 28 minutes.
And reportedly needed several doctors to help him recover.
So yes—the Olympic champion finished a marathon after being dosed with strychnine and brandy.
And somehow, the guy who rode in a car wasn't even the strangest part.
